title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Dirty is not the same question as unchanged
summary: Both commands that write into closed files placed their edits after checking whether the document was dirty. A file reloaded from disk is clean and different.

highlights.title: Clean and changed at the same time
highlights.description: A checkout or a stash pop reloads a document with new content and no dirty flag. The old offsets were then applied to it and landed on the wrong lines.

highlights.title: The bulk narrowing never looked
highlights.description: The command that makes every self only member private read the corpus copy and never consulted the open documents, so it always wrote at the measured position.

highlights.title: One rule, one place
highlights.description: Both commands call the same check now. Two copies of one condition is how one of them drifts, and this pair had already drifted.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: An edit is placed only when the open text still equals the text the scan measured.
A file that has moved on is skipped and counted, never edited at a guessed position.
